limits: Needs the network; known UniProt accessions only.
bio.jane/contract.noScientificClaim: Relays the remote service's own result unchanged; it computes no number of its own, so the service is the authority for what comes back.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which catalytic, binding and interface residues do member databases annotate in this protein's domains?

description: The individual catalytic, substrate-binding, metal-binding and interface residues a member database annotates INSIDE a domain, for a known protein. Takes a UniProt accession. This is what InterProScan itself does not return — its per-location site array comes back empty — so it is a separate lookup against InterPro, keyed to an entry whose sequence the residue numbers belong to.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

accession.description: UniProt accession, e.g. P00330. It must be the entry whose CURRENT sequence you mean: residues are numbered against it, so an accession for a protein that merely resembles yours puts a catalytic residue on the wrong amino acid.

name: lookup_residue_sites

residueCount.description: total annotated residues across every signature

signatures.description: per member-database signature: its accession, the database, its name, and each named site with every annotated residue and 1-based position
